description: Aggregator sources for the Best of the Internet obsession. The scout reads this file to find hunting grounds for hidden gems, and may append new sources it discovers. Each source is a URL or search pattern that tends to surface passionate, depth-first websites.

sources.notes: Meta-list of 'awesome' lists on GitHub — covers every niche imaginable
Marginalia Search — indie search engine that favors text-heavy, non-commercial sites
Wiby — search engine for the old web; surfaces handmade personal sites
Directory of active blogs organized by topic
Are.na — visual bookmarking for researchers and artists; deep rabbit holes
Show HN — people sharing what they built; filter for passion projects
MetaFilter — curated links from a community that values substance over clicks
Lobsters — invite-only tech link aggregator; less noise than HN
r/InternetIsBeautiful — dedicated to interesting, non-mainstream websites
r/DepthHub — long-form, in-depth content and discussion
Stumbled — StumbleUpon-style random discovery of small websites
href.cool — curated directory of weird and wonderful websites
Neal.fun — interactive visualizations and curiosity-driven projects (exemplar of the genre)
Personal Web directory — catalog of personal websites and digital gardens
Best of Show HN — curated archive of top Hacker News 'Show HN' posts by month and year
FOND/SOUND: deep-dive crate-digger blog by Diego Olivas with substantial Taiwan tag — long-form reviews of obscure Taiwanese, HK, Chinese records 1980s-90s.
Bandcamp Daily scene report on underground rock in Taipei — names specific bands, labels (White Wabbit Records), and albums across eras, useful as a hunting ground for Taiwanese music obsession
Mando Gap by Michael Hong — detailed critical rankings and essays on Mandopop albums by decade. Taiwan-focused, excellent for finding overlooked albums.
